reuse.why: The change reuses budget writes, spreadsheet reads, batching and undo wrappers, but shares only fragments of the category eligibility policy.

duplication.why: Category queries and exclusion guards remain repeated across month-wide actions, and the new spending action adds another copy.

placement.why: Budget policy stays in budget/actions.ts and method registration follows the existing budget/app.ts layering.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested budget actions, their registration, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate eligibility changes across six actions because the helpers do not own the complete selection decision.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth implements hidden-category eligibility inline instead of using the hiddenSql policy introduced elsewhere in the packet.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth expresses hidden-category exclusion as JavaScript guards while the other month-wide actions express the same policy through SQL.

abstraction_drift.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: hiddenSql introduces includeHiddenCategories and requireGroup, branches for inclusion and group-null handling, and is bypassed by copyPreviousMonth.
